A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIKAE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices report original time-series forecasting, satellite data-assimilation, ablation and lookback-length results.

after.justification: V2 retains original forecasting and assimilation results and adds initialization, hyperparameter, augmentation-size and linearity-loss experiments in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The main AIKAE architecture, delay embedding and assimilation procedure remain unchanged. Limited methodological additions include an explicitly untested stochastic IKAE variant with a variance encoder in Appendix B and weighted linearity-loss variants evaluated in F.2. These do not replace the principal deterministic method or its default loss.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the four ETT datasets, ECL, Traffic, Weather and Exchange, plus satellite forecasting on Fontainebleau and Orléans. The added studies use this existing coverage; stochastic modeling is discussed without experiments.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same competing methods: iTransformer, PatchTST, TimesNet and DLinear in Table 1, persistence in the extended table, and the existing comparator sets in the lookback, RevIN and satellite experiments. The new sensitivity studies concern internal configurations and ablations.

E3.justification: V1 reports fixed training hyperparameters, with batch sizes 4 for ETT and 32 otherwise. V2 Appendix D reports per-dataset, per-horizon searches over coupling-layer counts {3,4}, widths {128,256} and batch sizes {4,128,512}. This substantively revises the reported model-selection protocol. New hyperparameter, augmentation-size and loss-weight sweeps also introduce additional experimental controls.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained encoder/RevIN ablation and lookback study, v2 adds initialization sensitivity, learning-rate and architecture sensitivity, and ECL/Weather prediction cases in E.4–E.6. F.1–F.2 directly test how augmentation dimension and enforcement of augmentation linearity affect satellite forecasting.

E5.justification: V1 reports a fixed initialization for the main forecasting benchmark and five-instance averages without dispersion for satellite experiments. V2 Table 6 adds means and standard deviations across five separately trained initializations for IKAE and AIKAE on ECL and Weather at all four horizons. The existing satellite averaging practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Many IKAE/AIKAE scores change in Table 1 and the extended table under the revised tuning protocol. For example, Weather at horizon 720 changes from AIKAE MSE/MAE 0.363/0.354 to 0.317/0.333; this is not a same-setting method improvement. V2 also adds substantial sensitivity and ablation results. External baseline scores, satellite Table 2 and the original RevIN ablation scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B extends the existing change-of-variables discussion with Gaussian uncertainty propagation and a stochastic latent formulation. F.2 introduces the weighted linearity objective in Equation 23, and Section 3.1 adds a nullspace condition to the augmentation discussion. The principal Koopman and assimilation equations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central architectural contributions are retained. The conclusion qualifies v1's claim that AIKAE 'outperforms' IKAE to 'performs equally or better,' modestly narrowing the claimed performance advantage.

C2.justification: V2 interprets augmentation benefits as clearest on the larger ECL and Traffic datasets, with similar IKAE/AIKAE performance elsewhere. It adds a numerical-conditioning caveat to algebraic invertibility, an overfitting explanation for excessive augmentation, and a regularization explanation for enforcing augmentation linearity. These substantially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability limits.

D1.justification: New Appendices C–D document dataset characteristics and split sizes, data-loading code provenance, NICE coupling networks, nonlinearities, the augmentation MLP widths [256,128,32], parameter counts and search ranges. E.2–E.3 additionally disclose architecture and training controls for retained experiments. These are substantial reproducibility additions; the experiment-code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on flow conditioning, linear forecasting and channel independence, including Lee et al., Toner and Darlow, and Han et al., plus activation-function references. The overall research positioning remains stable. Several other reference changes are publication metadata updates for already cited works.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative and much of its wording are retained. V2 makes targeted explanatory and grammatical revisions, moves stochastic-modeling discussion into Appendix B, and reorganizes the expanded appendices. The added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale rewrite of the existing paper.

P2.justification: V2 adds multi-step and delay-embedding schematics, a hyperparameter-sensitivity figure, two forecasting case-study figures, and tables for dataset characteristics, seed variability and satellite ablations. Existing displays are retained or relocated under new numbering. These additions substantially expand the visual explanation and presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves reproducibility through Appendices C–D and strengthens evidence for the augmentation mechanism through capacity and loss ablations, sensitivity studies and five-seed uncertainty reporting. It also qualifies important interpretations and numerical-invertibility claims. A stale E.2 statement still links its unchanged ablation scores to the revised Table 1, and changed tuning limits direct interpretation of score gains. Nevertheless, the added methodological transparency and targeted validation provide a clear substantial overall improvement.
